column3: Near-verbatim parallel: no escape in the earth and no protector or helper apart from God.
Moses' limited authority over himself and his brother does not clarify universal inability to escape or find protection.
It joins God's dominion over heaven and earth with the exact denial of any protector or helper besides Him.
God's ownership of heaven and earth directly grounds the same denial of a protector or helper besides Him.
The flood's seizure of wrongdoing people supplies nearby narrative background for inescapable divine judgment.
It asks whether beings besides God can help their followers or help themselves, exposing the failure of alternative aid.
Nothing hidden in earth or heaven escapes God's knowledge, extending the focus's all-encompassing scope.
The next verse states the consequence of denying God's signs and meeting: despair of mercy and painful punishment.
Governance descending from heaven to earth portrays the connected realm within which escape is denied.
Nothing in earth or heaven is hidden from God, a knowledge parallel to the focus's comprehensive reach.
The claim that a gathered group can prevail contrasts with the focus's denial of independent help.
The shown dominion of heaven and earth supports the focus's claim that no realm lies outside divine power.
Creation and rule of heaven and earth are followed by denial of any protector or intercessor besides God.
Noah's rescue and the ark as a sign give only indirect nearby background about divine deliverance.
It explicitly denies that disbelievers can evade in the earth and names the unavoidable final destination.
It repeats that people cannot frustrate God, while locating the timing of the threatened event in His will.
The immediately preceding choice of punishment or mercy and return to God frames the focus's warning.
The claimed special friendship with God is tested, but it does not directly address the focus's universal warning.
Heaven and earth stand by His command, and His call brings people out of the earth, ruling out independent escape.
The denial that opponents will be helped gives a limited conflict setting for the focus's denial of help.
The oath by the heaven and its construction adds no focused clarification of escape or protection.
The promised event is certain and people cannot frustrate it, reinforcing the warning's inevitability.
The preceding call to worship and fear God supplies the immediate alternative to seeking protection elsewhere.
Naming God as Lord of heaven, earth, and what lies between supports the focus's cosmic range.
It repeats that the promised reality is true and cannot be frustrated, though without the protection clause.
The following verse rejects idols besides God and declares that no helpers will remain at judgment.
Acquisitions and protectors besides God prove useless before punishment, extending the failure of false protection.
It denies a protector or helper in the earth to those facing punishment in this life and the next.
The curse and disgrace of Pharaoh's people do not add a focused link to escape or protection.
God's dominion over heaven and earth and the return to Him support the focus's comprehensive authority.
Being seized while moving about, unable to frustrate God, concretizes the failure of escape.
The immediate idolatry warning denies idols provision and redirects worship and return to God.
God being sufficient as guide and helper gives a positive contrast but not the focus's universal warning.
God's command over earth, sea, and heaven displays the control that leaves no independent refuge.
The messenger's duty of clear delivery does not clarify the focus's warning.
The absence of protector and helper in enduring punishment gives an eschatological form of the focus's clause.
Unsupported worship besides God leaves wrongdoers without a helper, linking false devotion with abandonment.
The saying about patience and great fortune does not illuminate escape or protection.
Claiming divinity besides God leads to Hell, providing a consequence for the rival claim the focus excludes.
Worshippers and what they worship besides God enter Hell together, denying idols any saving role.
The nearby assertion of origination and re-creation establishes the power behind the focus's warning.
The question why alleged allies do not help exposes the collapse of mutual aid at judgment.
Signs in heaven, earth, rain, and winds indicate ordered divine action but only indirectly address escape.
Admission of believers among the righteous does not clarify the focus's warning.
All matters return to God whose way encompasses heaven and earth, giving a broad counterpart to no escape.
It closely combines inability to escape in the earth with having no protectors besides God.
Forgetting God and thereby forgetting oneself offers a moral warning but no direct protection parallel.
The Creator's names and the praise of heaven and earth add only general cosmic sovereignty.
Alleged beings besides God possess nothing in heaven or earth and give Him no support.
Travel through the earth to observe creation and resurrection supplies immediate context for divine capability.
Everything in heaven and earth belongs to God, who encompasses all things, supporting the focus's scope.
It closely pairs inability to escape in the earth with having no protectors besides God.
Universal death and return to God give nearby eschatological context without the focus's specific wording.
God's promised help to His messengers provides the positive counterpart to the denial of rival help.
It denies protectors besides God and then help, while warning against reliance on wrongdoers.
The shared mortality of the messenger and audience does not clarify escape or protection.
God's dominion over heaven and earth, absence of a partner, and measured creation support exclusive authority.
Reproach for earthly pride does not materially clarify the focus.
God's rescue of Abraham from fire demonstrates deliverance as His act within the surrounding narrative.
Lot's request for divine help gives a nearby positive use of the help denied apart from God.
At recompense no protector or helper besides God is found, though the setting is narrower than the focus.
Punishment descending from heaven on a corrupt town gives nearby narrative force to the heaven-and-earth range.
No one can shield people from God's intended harm or mercy, followed by the exact denial of protector and helper.
Not even an atom in earth or heaven escapes God's witnessing and record, supporting comprehensive reach.
The description of severe punishment adds no distinct clarification of escape or protection.
All that is in heaven and earth belongs to the Most High, supporting the focus's cosmic authority.
The subjection of what is in heaven and earth to human benefit still locates it within God's ordered gift.
Lot's migration to his Lord supplies only indirect nearby narrative contrast to seeking a refuge.
Divine help working through believers' hands shows that effective help remains sourced in God.
The divine sign in God's land and nearby punishment do not directly clarify escape or protection.
The later catalogue of seized peoples makes the surrounding warning concrete: no earthly setting was a refuge.
On that Day no close ally benefits another and no one is helped, giving a judgment-scene parallel.
Those calling on partners besides God follow conjecture, while all in heaven and earth belong to Him.
The question whether God is better than alleged partners gives only a general association contrast.
The challenge over creating heaven and earth supports the authority presupposed by the focus.
God alone knows the unseen of heaven and earth; none has a protector besides Him and none shares His judgment.
Abraham's descendants, prophecy, and reward do not clarify the focus's warning.
A punishment sent from the heaven challenges any sense of security from above.
The contrast between worldly provision and what is with God does not clarify escape or protection.
The clear sign left from Lot's town supports the immediate narrative of inescapable punishment.
Those cursed by God find no helper, but this adds little after the more direct helper parallels.
What is worshipped besides God cannot control provision from heaven or earth or act at all.
The sign of spouses, affection, and mercy has no focused relation to the warning.
Those striving to evade God's signs receive painful punishment, directly engaging the theme of futile evasion.
Wrongdoers having no protector or helper is a narrower repetition of the focus's final clause.
The messengers' rescue of Lot and his family shows divine deliverance within the nearby punishment narrative.
God holds the keys of heaven and earth, a compact image of exclusive access and control.
Alleged intercessors besides God can neither harm nor benefit and rest on claims unknown in heaven or earth.
Promised human support collapses under pressure, illustrating the unreliability of rival aid.
After flight, opponents find neither protector nor helper, a conflict-specific instance of abandoned support.
The splitting of heaven portrays cosmic upheaval but only indirectly relates to the focus.
The earth's violent shaking removes its apparent stability but adds only an indirect parallel.
Creation of heaven and earth being greater than creation of people supports the power behind the warning.
The heaven's breaking at the fulfilled promise gives an indirect image of unavoidable divine decree.
The conduct and privacy instruction does not clarify the focus's warning.
The changed, split heaven is a distant cosmic parallel without the protection or escape claim.
The household etiquette instruction has no focused relation to the candidate theme.
Mutual protection and help among believers describes a bounded human relation, contrasting with the focus's absolute claim.
All command belongs to God and death reaches people even at home, loosely reinforcing inescapability.
Believers become helpers of God and are strengthened by Him, showing the proper source and direction of help.
If God helps, none can overcome; if He forsakes, none can help afterward, directly defining the source of effective aid.
God's sufficient knowledge is paired with His sufficiency as protector and helper.
What is invoked besides God controls neither harm nor benefit, so it cannot supply the protection the focus denies.
When God touches a person with harm, none removes it except Him; mercy likewise cannot be withheld.
In sudden punishment, people are asked whether they would call on anyone other than God.
In distress people call on God alone, and He removes the harm if He wills, exposing the practical failure of associates.
No protector or intercessor can avert the requital of a soul that has been ruined by what it earned.
God is Creator of all things and guardian over all things, grounding the focus's absolute denial of outside protection.
The command to follow revelation affirms that there is no god but God and rejects turning toward associators.
No one removes harm God wills, and no one repels His bounty, directly ruling out an independent protector.
The messenger cannot control benefit or harm for himself except as God wills, setting a strict limit on creaturely power.
The alleged associates cannot help their worshippers and cannot help themselves.
Those invoked besides God cannot help people or help themselves.
Nothing befalls believers except what God decrees; He is their protector, specifying the proper reliance denied elsewhere.
Invoking what neither benefits nor harms besides God is identified as wrongdoing.
If God afflicts with harm none can remove it except Him, and none can repel His grace.
Every creature is held under God's control, leaving no autonomous route of escape.
The judgment belongs only to God; reliance is directed to Him alone despite human precaution.
Those who reject God's command have no protector besides Him.
Satan disclaims any coercive authority and admits that the wrongdoers have no rescue from punishment.
Those invoked besides God create nothing and are themselves created, unable to underwrite protection.
Those called besides God cannot remove harm or alter it.
When distress comes at sea, all those invoked besides God disappear from appeal.
The warning against being swallowed by land challenges any assumption of terrestrial safety.
The warning against a returning storm at sea denies confidence in escape by changing location.
Whomever God leaves astray has no protector besides Him.
The ruined garden owner has no party to help him besides God and cannot defend himself.
People take gods besides God for strength, introducing the false aim answered by the focus's denial of help.
Those alleged gods will reject their worship and become adversaries, reversing the hoped-for support.
The calf cannot control harm or benefit, disqualifying it as a source of rescue.
No one can shield people from the Most Merciful, directly challenging the possibility of a refuge from God.
Calling on what neither harms nor benefits besides God is named manifest error and its hoped-for aid is condemned.
The invoked being is called an evil protector and evil helper, directly contrasting the focus's pair of terms.
God holds the kingdom of everything and protects while none can be protected against Him.
The follow-up question exposes the contradiction of acknowledging God's lordship while still being deluded.
Gods besides Him create nothing and control neither harm, benefit, death, life, nor resurrection.
At judgment the worshippers are asked where their former objects of worship are before their inability to help is stated.
God answers the distressed, removes evil, and appoints succession on earth; the question rejects any rival god.
The summons to produce alleged partners makes their absence and incapacity public at judgment.
Everything perishes except God, and judgment belongs to Him, excluding any enduring rival refuge.
The admission that God created the heavens and earth and subjected the sun and moon grounds the focus's cosmic scope.
In danger at sea people call on God with exclusive devotion, then expose their inconsistency after rescue.
Security in the sanctuary is contrasted with insecurity around it, locating safety in God's grant rather than independent place.
No one can withhold mercy God opens or release what He withholds, directly excluding alternate control.
Gods besides Him cannot make intercession avail or save a person if the Most Merciful intends harm.
People take gods besides God hoping to be helped, making explicit the expectation the focus negates.
Those gods cannot help their worshippers even when worshippers stand as troops for them.
No one called besides God can remove harm He wills or withhold mercy He wills.
All intercession belongs to God, whose is the dominion of heaven and earth.
The wrongdoers have neither an intimate protector nor an intercessor whose word is accepted.
Whomever God leaves astray has no protector after Him.
The wrongdoers have no protectors besides God to help them, a close formulation of the focus's final clause.
Those invoked besides God possess no intercession except by truth and knowledge, sharply limiting rival claims.
Alleged partners are challenged to show what they created in earth or what share they possess in the heavens.
Gods taken as a means of nearness fail to help their worshippers and vanish from them.
God is protector of believers, while disbelievers have no protector.
The command to flee to God gives the positive direction implied when no other refuge exists.
Even angels' intercession benefits only after God's permission, limiting the strongest imaginable intermediary.
The challenge asks what army can help people against the Most Merciful, directly denying an alternative support force.
The messenger cannot control harm or right guidance for others independently.
No one can protect the messenger from God, and no refuge can be found apart from Him.
